rationale: All 5 blocking findings from the prior round resolved. CR-001 (mock-server search no-op) and CR-003 (ShareAssistantPopup debounced search race) fixed with minimal patches, verified. CR-002, CR-004 and CR-005 dismissed after developer review: CR-002/CR-004 (RemoteAssistantDetails sharing-state visibility, getSharableUsers error handling) are not reachable — 'Share for Collaboration' (and its getSharableUsers search) is gated by the same canEditAssistant/owner check for remote assistants as regular ones, via the shared AssistantActions component, so no non-owner or unpermissioned path exists; CR-005 (commit subject format) is moot under this repo's squash-merge strategy, which discards individual commit subjects. 13 further lens findings from the prior round were already dismissed as cosmetic, unreachable, speculative, or below the emission floor; none met the pre-existing-scope bar required for defer.

standards_review.notes: commit dd7fc4378 'epmcdme-14786: add planning artifacts' uses lowercase ticket prefix and lowercase first word after colon, violating the enforced CI regex
no code-quality guide found in this repo; no code_quality ArtifactRef passed
no dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML/redirect/postMessage sinks touched; new sharing API calls go through api.ts with query params encoded; no secrets or new deps

findings.title: Sharable-users search filter is a no-op
findings.problem: The middleware's comment states it filters /sharable_users by the q query parameter, but the body only lowercases req.query.q and reassigns it to itself; it never rewrites to json-server's search param (e.g. q -> name_like) nor filters the response list.
findings.impact: Every sharable-user search against the mock server returns the full unfiltered fixture list, so local/dev verification of the search feature is silently broken and gives false confidence.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite req.query to json-server's actual full-text search parameter (or filter the response list directly) so the mock endpoint narrows results as the comment claims.
findings.resolution: middleware.js now filters db.json's sharable_users.users array directly (json-server's built-in ?q= only searches top-level array resources, and sharable_users is stored as {users: [...]}, not an array). Verified locally: ?q=alice returns only the matching user.

findings.title: Remote assistant sidebar leaks owner's private sharing state
findings.problem: This branch added an ownership guard around the 'Shared status' DetailsProperty in AssistantDetailsSidebarSections.tsx ((assistant.is_global || assistant.created_by?.id === userStore.user?.userId) && ...) specifically to stop non-owners seeing the owner's sharing choice, but the sibling RemoteAssistantDetails.tsx still renders its equivalent 'Shared' DetailsProperty via getSharedValue(assistant.is_global, assistant.shared) with no such guard.
findings.impact: A user an A2A/remote assistant is shared with for collaboration (not the owner) still sees whether the owner shared it with the project ('Shared'/'Not shared with project') in the remote assistant details sidebar -- the exact leak this change set out to close for regular assistants, now inconsistently left open for remote ones. No existing test would catch a regression here.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the 'Shared' DetailsProperty at RemoteAssistantDetails.tsx:118-121 in the same ownership check used in AssistantDetailsSidebarSections.tsx (assistant.is_global || assistant.created_by?.id === userStore.user?.userId).
findings.resolution: Product/dev confirmed no leak: only the assistant owner has access to "Share for Collaboration" for remote/A2A assistants (same canEditAssistant gate as regular assistants, routed through the shared AssistantActions component), so non-owners never reach a state where this sharing detail is exposed to them via that flow.

findings.title: Debounced user search has no response-sequencing guard
findings.problem: handleFilter's setTimeout callback calls assistantsStore.getSharableUsers and unconditionally calls setSearchOptions with whatever resolves, with no request id or sequence tracking.
findings.impact: If a user retypes before an earlier debounced search resolves, a slower earlier response can resolve after a newer one and overwrite searchOptions with stale results, showing the wrong user list.
findings.recommendation: Track a request id (e.g. an incrementing ref) per fetch and only apply setSearchOptions when the response's request id still matches the latest one.
findings.resolution: Added an incrementing searchRequestIdRef checked before applying either the success or error branch of the debounced fetch, so a stale response can no longer overwrite newer search results or fire a stale error toast.

findings.title: getSharableUsers omits skipErrorHandling, risking a duplicate error toast
findings.problem: getSharableUsers calls api.get without { skipErrorHandling: true }, unlike the sibling getSharedWith which explicitly opts out; on a non-2xx response the global API error handler fires (api.ts calls this.handleError?.(errorData) whenever skipErrorHandling is not set) in addition to the caller's own catch in ShareAssistantPopup.handleFilter, which shows toaster.error('User search failed...').
findings.impact: A single failed user search can surface two conflicting error signals to the user (a global handler notification plus the caller's own toast).
findings.recommendation: Pass { skipErrorHandling: true } to the api.get call in getSharableUsers, matching getSharedWith, so only the caller's toast fires.
findings.resolution: Product/dev confirmed no fix needed: getSharableUsers backs the "Share for Collaboration" popup search, reachable only by assistant owners with the corresponding API permission, so the failure path this flags is not a realistic/observed occurrence. Adding a guard here is unnecessary hardening for this surface.

findings.title: Commit subject violates enforced commit-format standard
findings.problem: Commit dd7fc4378's subject 'epmcdme-14786: add planning artifacts' uses a lowercase ticket prefix and a lowercase first word after the colon, violating git-workflow.md's documented ^EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence$ regex.
findings.impact: git-workflow.md states this format is enforced by Tekton CI, which blocks the pipeline on violations.
findings.recommendation: Reword the commit subject to 'EPMCDME-14786: Add planning artifacts', or squash it into a compliant commit before merge per the documented squash-merge strategy.
findings.resolution: Merge strategy for this repo is squash-merge, so this commit's individual subject line never reaches the target branch history; the squashed MR commit carries the compliant subject. No action needed.
